subject.title: [Bug]: Compaction retry creates orphan fork in parentId chain (dead-end branch breaks chain reconstruction)

question: Should OpenClaw repair same-parent compaction retry forks by dropping dead-end compaction entries during session-file repair, or should the recovery policy preserve rows and use a different reconciliation marker/path?
rationale: The bug is source-backed, but the proposed fix changes persisted session data and needs an explicit maintainer-owned recovery policy before merge.

options.title: Approve compaction-only repair
options.body: Refresh and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/79635 as the fix path, with the invariant that only dead-end compaction-vs-compaction retry losers are removed.

options.title: Require non-deleting recovery
options.body: Ask for a replacement design that marks or supersedes the orphan branch without removing persisted rows.

options.title: Defer repair
options.body: Keep the issue open without landing the candidate and accept that parent-chain reconstruction remains vulnerable until a narrower policy is approved.

recommendation.title: Approve compaction-only repair
recommendation.body: Refresh and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/79635 as the fix path, with the invariant that only dead-end compaction-vs-compaction retry losers are removed.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership evidence points to this author as the best available routing candidate for session repair policy in the checked-out history.
